newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak FinMin sets one-year bond auction on Aug 5.
newsitem.headline: Slovak FinMin sets one-year bond auction on Aug 5.

text.p: The Slovak Finance Ministry said on Tuesday it would auction an unspecified tranche of one-year state bonds on August 5, with a fixed coupon of 11.00 percent.
The National Bank of Slovakia (NBS) will conduct the American-style auction, each with a 100,000 crown ($2,860) nominal value, the ministry said in a statement.
Average yield in the last successful auction of one-year state bonds on July 22 rose to 17.8 percent from 16.812 percent in the previous sale of similar bonds on July 8.
The ministry does not set an amount on offer in state securities auctions or a minimum or maximum limit price on bids.
It mainly uses T-bills and state bonds to cover the state budget deficit, which widened to 17.790 billion crowns as of July 8, 1997. That compares with 7.177 billion crowns in the January-May period.
